entries.title: Chat follows a request for a detailed answer
entries.body: Chat is told to keep its answers to about 300 words. That limit no longer applies when you ask outright for a detailed, in-depth or step-by-step answer, or for the long version, so a walk-through you asked for is less likely to come back cut short. Asking only for a summary still gets a short one.

entries.title: Green buttons send, red buttons leave
entries.body: More forms colour their buttons the way Feedback already did: green for the one that sends or saves, red for the one that leaves without saving. You will see it on sharing and private-link confirmations, Start again, the profile panel, saving or discarding a note, and renaming a chat or editing a question.

entries.title: We record when your account opens articles
entries.body: Spideryarn keeps a record of when your account opens its articles, tied to the account rather than to any one article, so we can see how often the app is used. The privacy policy has a new line saying so. The record starts with this version; nothing earlier was filled in.

entries.title: Structure is less likely to misplace a section
entries.body: When building an article's Structure, the AI sometimes named a passage that did not exist as the start of a section, so the section could begin in the wrong place. It now picks each start in a way that makes this mistake less likely. The change applies to articles whose Structure is built from now on.
